name: split-reveal
summary: A display pull-quote split into lines and words by anime.js, with a slow looping wave: lines drift and colour-shift on a 100ms stagger while the words inside each line breathe.

duration.description: Length of one half of the wave, in ms. Upstream's timeline default; it alternates, so a full cycle is twice this.

loopDelay.description: Pause between wave repetitions, in ms. Upstream's timeline default.

stagger.description: Delay added per line, and per word within a line, in ms. Upstream's stagger value on both tracks.

deviations.what: The second addEffect -- the one that scatters words to utils.random(-50, 50) on pointerenter and caches their coordinates -- is dropped, along with the tweaks GUI panel that drives split, revert, tidy-up and debug.
deviations.why: The scatter makes the copy unreadable on hover, which is the wrong trade for a section a site ships to readers, and it only makes sense next to the GUI's 'Tidy up' button. The GUI is an examples-page dependency (tweaks/gui) that a generated site has no way to load.

deviations.what: The colour the lines animate from is var(--fx-accent) rather than upstream's var(--sega-1).
deviations.why: --sega-1 is a palette variable from the anime examples' own stylesheet. The contract prefixes custom properties --fx-, and the section declares this one so the resting state and the animation read the same value.

deviations.what: splitText is given the section's own paragraph element instead of the selector 'p'.
deviations.why: The example owns its whole page; an effect is one section among several and may appear twice on a page. Passing the element the section holds is what keeps two mounts from splitting each other's copy.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion the text is not split at all.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest. It also leaves the copy as one selectable, screen-reader-plain block, which is strictly better than a split one that never moves.
